title: Import a document
description: Import TXT, DOCX, RTF, or text-based PDF files locally, review the extracted text, and save it as a script.
body:
# Import a document

**Import Document** turns one local TXT, DOCX, RTF, or text-based PDF into editable plain text. Extraction happens on the device in a disposable worker. It does not upload the file, execute document scripts, render imported HTML, fetch embedded resources, or preserve rich styling and images.

## Before you begin

- Have one file in `.txt`, `.docx`, `.rtf`, or `.pdf` format.
- Keep the input at or below 10 MiB. Expanded document content is limited to 32 MiB, PDFs to 500 pages, and saved output to 500,000 UTF-16 characters.
- Know that image-only or scanned PDFs need OCR or copied text in another application first. Quickque does not perform OCR.
- Keep a full backup via **Settings & backups** → **Export Full Backup** if the import is part of a destructive rewrite. Import creates a new script only after you choose **Save as Script**.

## Steps

1. In the library sidebar, select **Import document**. You can also drop one file on the library or on the import drop area. Quickque accepts one file at a time.

2. Choose the file. The dialog shows **Extracting text...** while the local worker reads it. If you chose the wrong file, select **Cancel** before extraction completes.

3. When extraction finishes, read the review dialog rather than assuming the layout survived. The title is editable under **Script Title** and the content is editable under **Extracted Text**.

4. Correct the title and clean up paragraphs, columns, headers, or footers. For PDF columns, check that the reading order makes sense. The review may show a note that formatting, images, and layout were removed.

5. Select **Save as Script**. Quickque writes the new script and selects it only after the local library accepts the write.

![Quickque library in the browser preview](/images/library.webp)

*Browser preview only: the screenshot shows the destination library; it does not verify native file-picker or Finder-drop behavior.*

## Expected result

A new script appears in the library with the reviewed title and plain text. Rich styling, images, document objects, and layout are intentionally absent. Canceling the picker, extraction, or review creates no script. If local storage rejects the save, the review remains open and the prior library and selection are preserved.

## Format boundaries

- **TXT:** decoded as text.
- **RTF:** text, paragraphs, tabs, line breaks, Unicode escapes, and supported Windows single-byte code pages are read. Pictures, objects, fields, metadata, and HTML destinations are skipped.
- **DOCX:** paragraphs and runs from the WordprocessingML document are read locally. Encrypted or malformed archives and unsupported XML fail explicitly.
- **PDF:** text operators are read with a bundled local PDF parser. Columns, positioned words, images, scans, and rich layout are not retained; line breaks and reading order depend on the source PDF.

## Troubleshooting

- **Unsupported file type:** select a single `.txt`, `.docx`, `.rtf`, or `.pdf` file. Renaming an unrelated binary file does not make it supported.
- **The PDF is blank:** it may be scanned or image-only. Copy text from another tool or run OCR elsewhere, then import the resulting text.
- **The PDF columns are scrambled:** edit the extracted text in the review step and check the complete script before presenting. Quickque cannot promise visual PDF reading order.
- **The file is too large or extraction times out:** reduce the input or split it into smaller documents within the documented limits. Do not expect silent truncation.
- **I dropped multiple files:** the UI accepts one file only. Repeat the operation for each file and review each result separately.
- **Save as Script is disabled or fails:** the title and extracted text must be nonblank, and the output must be within 200 title characters and 500,000 text characters. A storage failure is reported instead of claiming the script was saved.
- **Finder drop does not work in a Mac build:** native Finder drop and packaged WKWebView behavior still need Mac verification. Use the file picker while investigating and record the result rather than treating browser behavior as proof.
- **I need to undo a saved import:** use **Settings & backups** → **Export Full Backup** before moving the imported script to **Trash**. To move that backup into another origin, use **Import Backup JSON**; import is additive and keeps the destination's selection and sort mode.
